name: Bright Studio - Soho - Central HK
description:
Our bright studio apartment is perfect for visiting Hong Kong Island.
Located on a quiet street 10 minutes walk from Soho and the escalator and with all the amenities you need its a perfect space for you to relax after seeing the sights.
host_about:
Hi Everyone,

my Wife and I have this little apartment for friends and family which we let to travelers to Hong Kong when its free.  

We like to look after people and ensure that they enjoy their stay in Hong Kong.  We have someone who will visit every other day to keep the place clean and tidy.  

We can arrange travel cards, maps and local SIMs for you upon arrival if you need and will meet you at the door or provide a self check in option depending on your needs.

We will be available on the phone during your stay to help with whatever you need and make sure that you enjoy your stay.  If you need an unlocked phone for your stay we are happy to lend you one.

The apartment is 5 minutes walk from Soho and the Elevator and it puts you right in the middle of the main bar/restaurant area of Hong Kong Island.  You will not want to spend much time in the apartment as everything is so close by.  However, for those days when you just want to sit and relax though we have a pile of DVDs and can lend you a few games if you need.

And, if you are a sailor, we are members of the RHKYC and can make some introductions if you want.

hope to see you in Hong Kong soon.

Darren and Annalisa

host_about:
I am Chinese & was brought up in the UK and born in Malaysia, but lived in Hong Kong for over 30 years now.

My childhood was spent mainly travelling around with my family of  5 siblings as my father was stationed at several British Army bases around Malaysia, Singapore, Hong Kong & the UK. Therefore, I enjoy travelling & meeting people of different cultures.

I have travelled to Europe & the States during my student days & most of my family members have now settled in the States & the UK.

The Mahjong takes its name from a traditional game that dates back to late Qing dynasty when locals gathered together over a table of 144 game pieces to play and while away the days. Today, the game has evolved into a national pastime and is played everywhere – at home, in the park, even dedicated mahjong parlours around the city. There are various legends on how the game got its name – one being the Mahjong sparrow it was named after, for its petite yet agile body that resembled the game pieces.

I love to laugh out loud, perhaps because of a thought that has made me happy, to contemplate on this world and the part I play in it, to feel salty ocean water on my legs, to appreciate life's little nuances, have immense gratitude for the life I have, and to dance with abandon. 

I have been to London, UK, once, and loved it. Mauritius twice (late 90's and early 2000's) - love the place, the people, the beauty of the island. I traveled to Australia (Perth) for 5 days in 2013 (met up with my dear Aunt and traveled to New Norcia), and had my first Airbnb experience (it was lovely, with friendly hosts), and also visited New Zealand (Auckland - 2013), where my brother and his wife and family live (loved my time with them and visited Wellington for a few days too, which was great). I have also spent time in Muni-ki-reti, India, at the Divine Life Society, twice (2011 and 2015), which was a wonderful experience.

I moved to Hong Kong at the end of September 2016, and find life here very interesting. Since moving over, I have visited Koh Samui, Thailand twice (October and December 2018), Hoi An in Vietnam (November 2018), Macau (many times), Melaka, Malaysia (April 2019), Phuket, Thailand (May 2019), Morocco (July 2019)  and of course have had many trips back home. I continue to look forward to other destinations.

I love to meet new people, listen to their stories, and enjoy interesting conversations. I also enjoy quiet time. As a yogi, I try and use all experiences to better my life, and try to learn through every interaction. Sometimes people click so well, that shared time is wonderful and seamless, and the connection lasts long after one has said goodbye. 

I love connecting with humanity, whether it be in the form of people or animals. I find nature incredibly uplifting, invigorating, and soul enhancing, always. 

I am friendly, easy going, love to soak in every minute of each day, and am grateful for the opportunities that come my way in life, in which ever way it presents itself.

What I try and keep uppermost in mind always is this: Be the change you want to see in the world; Think before you speak

Happy days to you :)

Welcome to Hong Kong and hope to see you soon!

host_about:
Founded by backpackers and soultrippers, The Mahjong is the result of years of pursuing a dream to establish a comfortable boutique hostel that offers cultural immersion in addition to a social exchange for travelers to meet and swap stories.

The Mahjong takes its name from a traditional game that dates back to late Qing dynasty when locals gathered together over a table of 144 game pieces to play and while away the days. Today, the game has evolved into a national pastime and is played everywhere – at home, in the park, even dedicated mahjong parlours around the city. There are various legends on how the game got its name – one being the Mahjong sparrow it was named after, for its petite yet agile body that resembled the game pieces.

host_about:
你好,我係Sam,是土生土長香港人｡從小到大,我都喜歡背包旅行, 以前覺得香港天空好小, 好羨慕外國的天空好大,四圍都有綠油油的森林和草地｡望住天空,就好想走去看看天空另一面的世界是怎樣｡15歲那年暑假決定出走一次,帶住背包,一個人闖蕩西藏旅行45日,從此,一發不可收拾!

記得最激一次,是大學跟四位同學從廣州徒步到內蒙古｡經歷70多日的艱苦路程,回憶畢身難忘｡每一次旅程,除了令人難忘的風景,跟當地人的交流互動,都是每一次旅行都獨一無二的重要原素｡所以我希望透過開辦民宿旅館,認識世界各地不同的客人,希望我可以代表香港,歡迎每一位來到我們家的客人｡讓大家感受香港人這個城市的人情味和好客之道｡

host_about:
Hi, 我是Ibis, 小名叫”雲雲”。我在香港長大，最初懷著成為牙醫的夢想，雖未能如願，卻也在牙科護士的崗位上耕耘過。以往的日子，不過是在繁華都市裡機械地重復著上班、下班、吃飯、睡覺，彷彿只是為了生存而奔波。

直到一次香格里拉之旅，那裡濃郁的人情味與獨特的藏族文化深深觸動了我。後來的兩年，我踏上了旅遊博主之路，在不同的風景里感悟生活。在這個過程中，我愈發覺得，自己出生的香港，同樣藏著無數值得被探尋的美好。

如今，我決定在香港發展旅遊民宿，希望以”家”的溫暖為底色，融入這座城市的獨特韻味，為每一位旅人提供一個別樣的棲息之所。我有豐富的旅行經歷，也懂得將心比心，會像朋友一樣親切地接待每一位客人，願你在這裡收穫一段難忘的旅程！

name: (HK) WanChai, 20meters from MTR, 2Bedrooms
description:
Just 20meters from WanChai MTR exit A1. Very convenience, located at Lockhart Road, the heart of WanChai district.

This pulsating district has its share of good-time joints and exotic nightlife, but the real news is its thrilling evolution into one of the city’s coolest, most dynamic areas, with a heady mix of old and new, and East meets West, and where hip bars and happening restaurants mix with old tenement buildings and hidden temples among the district’s towering skyscrapers.
host_about:
Hi, 我是Ibis, 小名叫”雲雲”。我在香港長大，最初懷著成為牙醫的夢想，雖未能如願，卻也在牙科護士的崗位上耕耘過。以往的日子，不過是在繁華都市裡機械地重復著上班、下班、吃飯、睡覺，彷彿只是為了生存而奔波。

直到一次香格里拉之旅，那裡濃郁的人情味與獨特的藏族文化深深觸動了我。後來的兩年，我踏上了旅遊博主之路，在不同的風景里感悟生活。在這個過程中，我愈發覺得，自己出生的香港，同樣藏著無數值得被探尋的美好。

如今，我決定在香港發展旅遊民宿，希望以”家”的溫暖為底色，融入這座城市的獨特韻味，為每一位旅人提供一個別樣的棲息之所。我有豐富的旅行經歷，也懂得將心比心，會像朋友一樣親切地接待每一位客人，願你在這裡收穫一段難忘的旅程！

name: Garden townhouse within walking distance to beach
description:
Have fun at this stylish place. A home away from home that is bright and breezy.

Free Wi fi and all utilities provided, and free access to the pool to cool off during the hot summer season, or take a beach stroll along the promenade to many international restaurants and cafes, close to amenities such as the ice skating rink, shopping mall and supermarket.

Guest bedrooms provided with linen and towels, as well as making use of washing machine and dryer, kitchen facilities and balcony.
host_about:
I am Chinese & was brought up in the UK and born in Malaysia, but lived in Hong Kong for over 30 years now.

My childhood was spent mainly travelling around with my family of  5 siblings as my father was stationed at several British Army bases around Malaysia, Singapore, Hong Kong & the UK. Therefore, I enjoy travelling & meeting people of different cultures.

I have travelled to Europe & the States during my student days & most of my family members have now settled in the States & the UK.

I preferred to settle in Hong Kong as the place is as vibrant as the people who play hard, & work hard here. Hong Kong has a 'buzz' you cannot find anywhere else in the world. 

It has been interesting living through the changes from the British colonial days to the handover back to China, & being part of 'history', & revealing of the versatility of the people here to the changing times to not just strive, but thrive in various aspects of their lives & livelihood.

Hong Kong brings out the best & worst in you... ^_^
